scope: Proposition 5.4 of the manuscript “Quaternionic division points on curves in the Siegel threefold” (preprints/Quaternionic-Division-Points-on-Curves-in-the-Siegel-Threefold-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 016 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e11b4b068502ced9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a selected marked target as in Proposition 5.2, each applicable list above, formed from a nonempty selected group of places, satisfies the all-branch nonidentity hypothesis of Theorem 3.1. More precisely, let W be any irreducible algebraic subvariety of the indicated affine ambient conditions which contains the target and on which a is nonconstant. On every branch over the generic point of every component of W ∩ {a = 0}, at least one equation in the applicable list, including the chart equations, is not an identity.
